picture.note: Area fractions in this map were measured on the picture rectangle above, not on the full coded frame. Letterbox and pillarbox bars were removed first.

area_windows.name: bt1702-screen
area_windows.source: ITU-R BT.1702-3 Annex 1 Guideline 1, 25% of the displayed screen area

area_windows.name: room-10deg
area_windows.source: 10 degrees from WCAG 2.2, sized by TV diagonal and seat distance

exceptions_not_implemented: WCAG fine balanced pattern exception (white noise, checkerboards under 0.1 degree). Content the exception would excuse is still reported.
profile.name: broadcast

pattern_rule.contrast_condition: the same difference as a potentially harmful flash in Guideline 1, which is this profile's general_flash rule. No luminance number of its own.
pattern_rule.exemption: a pattern that obviously flows smoothly across, into or out of the screen in one direction. Applied only when the flow is unambiguous, and every application is listed in pattern_exemptions.
pattern_rule.not_a_wcag_finding: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.1 does not cover regular patterns. A pattern segment is never a WCAG finding and never changes a WCAG verdict.
pattern_rule.source: ITU-R BT.1702-3 Attachment 1 to Annex 1 (informative), which says these criteria are used by some administrations (SPEC_SOURCES section 8). The bar to bar difference is Guideline 1's flash difference, reused from general_flash.

tuning.what_these_are: detector tuning, not thresholds. BT.1702-3 gives no persistence time, no stripe width and no spatial frequency band, so none is used as a threshold. See flashmap/docs/SPEC_SOURCES.md implementation decision 9.

pattern_rule.uncertain_motion_rule: an uncertain motion class takes the changing area limit, never the stationary one, and never the exemption

profile.pattern_rule_source: ITU-R BT.1702-3 Attachment 1 to Annex 1 (informative), which says these criteria are used by some administrations (SPEC_SOURCES section 8). The bar to bar difference is Guideline 1's flash difference, reused from general_flash.

red_flash.source: BT.1702-3 calls a transition to or from a saturated red harmful but gives no numbers, so the WCAG 2.2 and ISO 9241-391 working definition is reused (SPEC_SOURCES sections 4 and 5)

rules_not_implemented: the HDR branch, Michelson contrast 1/17 above 160 cd/m2
the 360 ms and 334 ms leading edge allowance, which could only excuse flashes
any persistence time, stripe width or spatial frequency band for Guideline 2. BT.1702-3 gives none, so none is used as a threshold
profile.title: ITU-R BT.1702-3 Annex 1 Guideline 1, standard dynamic range only

summary.pattern_findings_are_not_wcag: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.1 does not cover regular patterns. A pattern segment is an extra hide from an informative ITU recommendation, never a WCAG finding, and `flash_pass` is the only verdict a WCAG claim may be read from.
summary.pattern_rule_source: ITU-R BT.1702-3 Attachment 1 to Annex 1 (informative), which says these criteria are used by some administrations (SPEC_SOURCES section 8). The bar to bar difference is Guideline 1's flash difference, reused from general_flash.
